findings.issue: The masked date field's own value is drawn underneath its calendar icon, so the day is unreadable. `.w-field-adornment` is absolutely positioned at `inset-inline-end: 4px` with `width: 30px` over the control, but `.w-field-control` only declares `padding-inline: 12px` — no allowance for the adornment. Because `.w-field-control` also sets `unicode-bidi: plaintext`, a typed date is an LTR run and is laid out from the field's inline-end (= left, in this RTL app) edge, i.e. exactly where the icon sits. Measured live in the running host on /gallery: the input box starts at x=55.2 so its text starts at x=67.2, while the adornment spans x=59.2–89.2 — a 22px overlap covering the first two glyphs. Two screenshots (light and dark theme, value «12/09/2026») show the calendar glyph painted on top of «12». The same geometry hits the Password variant (eye button at x=599.2–629.2 over text starting at x=607.2; the crop shows the eye on the first masked dot). The reference design keeps the adornment clear of the value (design/exports/light/M/M12 — مصروف — الإدخال.png: the calendar icon sits well inside the inline-end margin with «12/09/2026 — 10:24» beside it, never under it). Pre-existing from B0.5 rather than introduced by this package, but it is the very component this package polishes and it only becomes visible once the field holds a value — which is why the earlier review, which looked at the empty field (its Arabic placeholder «يوم/شهر/سنة» is RTL and therefore starts at the opposite edge), did not catch it.
findings.fix: Reserve the adornment's track on the adorned variants. In src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WInput.razor add a modifier class to both `<input>` elements inside `.w-field-control-wrap` — `class="w-field-control @(Type is WInputType.Date or WInputType.Password ? "w-field-control--adorned" : null)"` (lines 27 and 33) — and in src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WInput.razor.css add, after the `.w-field-control` rule, `.w-field-control--adorned { padding-inline-end: 40px; }` (30px adornment + 4px inset + 6px gap). Do not widen `padding-inline` globally, which would also shift the textarea and the unadorned fields. Then relaunch Wakeel.Desktop with --start-url=/gallery, type 12092026 into التاريخ and seven characters into كلمة المرور, and re-measure: `input.getBoundingClientRect().x + parseFloat(getComputedStyle(input).paddingInlineEnd)` must be at or past the adornment's far edge in both themes.

findings.issue: Finding 1 of verify-design-split.json is fixed exactly as prescribed (line 156 now reads `if (formatted == (Value ?? string.Empty))`) but the underlying defect survives one keystroke later on a genuinely unbound Date field. On `<WInput Type="WInputType.Date" />` with no @bind-Value and no ValueChanged, `Value` stays null forever, so Blazor's `value="@Value"` attribute never changes and its diff never touches the DOM. First keystroke 'a': formatted "" equals (null ?? "") — the branch fires and the DOM is corrected, which is what the new bUnit test covers. But type '1' then 'a': formatted is "1", the guard compares "1" against "", the branch is skipped, ValueChanged goes nowhere and the 'a' stays on screen; typing 'b' next leaves "1ab". The guard is asking "does the reformatted text equal the parameter?" when the question it needs answered is "will Blazor's next diff rewrite the DOM?", and for an unbound field the answer is always no. Not reachable from the shipped pages today (Gallery.razor:35 is the only Date usage and it binds `_dateValue`), but WInput is a shared design-system component that other packages will consume.
findings.fix: Stop branching on the parameter and make the post-render pass authoritative. In OnDateInputAsync, alongside `_pendingCaret = newCaret;` add `_pendingValue = formatted;` (new field `private string? _pendingValue;`) and delete the whole `if (formatted == (Value ?? string.Empty)) { ... }` block including its setInputValue call. In OnAfterRenderAsync, replace the `wakeelUi.setCaretPosition` call with `await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("wakeelUi.setInputValue", _dateRef, _pendingValue ?? string.Empty, caret);` and clear `_pendingValue` next to `_pendingCaret`. Writing the mask output to the DOM after Blazor's diff is idempotent when Blazor already wrote the same string, and it covers the bound, unbound and rejected-character cases with one path; keep `wakeelUi.setCaretPosition` in app.js only if another caller appears, otherwise drop it. Update tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/Components/WInputTests.cs accordingly and add a test that renders WInput with Type=Date, no Value and no ValueChanged, Inputs "1" then "1a", and asserts the second Input invokes wakeelUi.setInputValue with ("1", 1).

findings.issue: Icon-only buttons in the design system carry an aria-label but no `title`, so no hover tooltip appears — the brief requires a tooltip on every icon-only button. Enumerated live on /gallery: nine buttons render no text, and all nine have aria-label and `title=null` (w-sidebar-sync-refresh «تحديث», two w-btn--icon «الإشعارات»/«التقويم», w-btn--icon «تحديث», w-btn-split-caret with neither label nor title, WInput's w-field-adornment «إظهار كلمة المرور», two w-pager-nav «السابق»/«التالي», w-menu-trigger «خيارات إضافية»). The WButton split-caret is the worst case: no aria-label and no title at all. System-wide and pre-existing, not introduced by this package; WInput's own calendar adornment is correctly a `<span aria-hidden="true">` and needs nothing. Raised because the review brief asks for it explicitly.
findings.fix: Mirror each existing aria-label into a `title` on the same element so the Arabic label is both announced and shown on hover: WInput.razor line 38 becomes `... aria-label="@(_revealed ? Ar.Fields.HidePassword : Ar.Fields.ShowPassword)" title="@(_revealed ? Ar.Fields.HidePassword : Ar.Fields.ShowPassword)"`, and the same one-attribute addition in WButton.razor (which must also gain an Arabic label for the split caret, e.g. a new `Ar.Buttons.MoreActions`), WTopBar.razor, WPager.razor, WSidebar.razor and WMenu.razor. Worth scheduling as its own polish package rather than folding into this one.
